messages:
deploy-bot: :warning: ALERT: GPUs running low in asia-west1 (pending_gpus=42) — https://console.example/alerts/12345
maria (eng-infra): seeing this now. a bunch of inference jobs pending, but CA isn't creating new nodes in asia-west1-b/c zonal quotas are hit.
chris (eng-sre): I pulled autoscaler logs:
```
E 2026-09-02T08:12:45Z cluster-autoscaler: Failed to scale up: failed to create instance: googleapi: Error 403: resourceQuotaExhausted -> quota exceeded for region asia-west1 (TYPE_QUOTA)
```
maria (eng-infra): exactly. GCP returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for asia-west1-a/b/c. CA keeps retrying but GKE can't provision.
sandip (eng-platform): our fallback cluster in us-central has capacity but routing is per-cluster via fleet-router and service-dns. we can failover at request-level, not pod-level. latency for some customers will spike though.
anya (oncall): for critical inference routes (model=redwood-small-prod) we should failover. non-critical batch jobs can wait. who owns fleet-router changes?
sandip (eng-platform): I can push a temporary routing rule: prefer asia-west1, fallback to us-central with sticky sessions off. small change to the controller. but we need to avoid double-cost (ingress + egress).
maria (eng-infra): also CA flags: we currently have --balance-similar-node-groups enabled and node pools across zones are treated as similar. when one zone is quota-exhausted CA tries to rebalance instead of scaling the other zones. disabling that flag might let us scale us-central faster.
chris (eng-sre): CA also enforces max-node-provision-time=15m; if provisioning hangs because of quota it keeps failing. We should surface clearer errors to devs.
anya (oncall): what about creating a dedicated fallback nodepool labelled redwood/gpu=fallback-us? terraform quick patch?
maria (eng-infra): terraform patch ready + manual apply will take ~10m. But we need nodepool labels & taints so only fallback workloads land there:
```
resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu-fallback-us" {
  name = "gpu-fallback-us"
  node_config { labels = { "redwood/gpu-type" = "nvidia-a100" "redwood/role" = "fallback" } }
  management { auto_repair = true }
  autoscaling { min_node_count = 0 max_node_count = 20 }
}
```
sandip (eng-platform): add a pod affinity rule for production pods: prefer nodes with redwood/region=asia-west1, then tolerate fallback via nodeSelector + toleration for redwood/role=fallback.
chris (eng-sre): FYI CA log showing why it didn't scale other region:
```
I0902 08:14:02.345 autoscaler: NodeGroup "asia-west1-ndp" can't be increased because of quota constraints in region asia-west1
```
maria (eng-infra): action plan I propose:
1) apply terraform to create gpu-fallback-us nodepool (owner: me)
2) patch fleet-router to add fallback route for model=redwood-small-prod (owner: sandip)
3) temporarily set cluster-autoscaler flag --balance-similar-node-groups=false on asia clusters (owner: chris)
4) increase alert verbosity so quota errors show up in dedicated channel (owner: anya)
ill add timings as I apply.
sandip (eng-platform): noticed one more caveat: some pods request strict topology key topology.kubernetes.io/zone, CA respects that and won't place pods cross-zone if nodeAffinity prevents it. we might need to relax PodTopologySpread for the short term.
anya (oncall): risk: relaxing topology increases single-AZ blast radius if a zone goes down. but given quota outage it's acceptable for 1 hour failover window.
chris (eng-sre): pushing CA flag change now, will roll restart the autoscaler deployment. I'll annotate with rollback window.
deploy-bot: Job 9876: terraform apply started by maria (plan -> apply)
maria (eng-infra): terraform apply done, gpu-fallback-us nodepool created (10 nodes booting). kube nodes appearing:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l redwood/role=fallback -o wide
NAME                                         STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gke-redwood-us-fallback-1a                   Ready    <none>   1m    v1.27.3
gke-redwood-us-fallback-1b                   Ready    <none>   1m    v1.27.3
```
maria (eng-infra): patched pod tolerations for prod deployment to allow fallback nodes (rolled <model>-deploy)
sandip (eng-platform): fleet-router patch deployed: fallback path active. TTLs lowered to avoid long stickiness.
chris (eng-sre): autoscaler flag disabled and restarted. CA logs now show attempts to scale other nodegroups in other regions.
```
I 2026-09-02T08:27:10Z cluster-autoscaler: Scale-up: adding 4 nodes to group us-central-gpu
```
maria (eng-infra): pending GPUs drained from 42 -> 0 in ~12m. latency to fallback region increased p95 from 80ms -> 210ms for routed traffic.
anya (oncall): reopening support runbook entry to document manual fallback steps and risks (I added a checklist).
sandip (eng-platform): follow-up: we should implement an automated region-fallback controller: a small service that watches GPU quota metrics per region and flips fleet-router policies + terraform apply to create fallback nodepools automatically.
maria (eng-infra): agree. also request quotas proactively: submitted GCP quota increase ticket for asia-west1 GPUs (case 9901).
chris (eng-sre): final note: add a gating policy so CA can scale across region-paired nodegroups instead of trying to rebalance similar groups in a single region. I'll draft an RFC.
anya (oncall): thanks all. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and escalate if node provisioning errors reappear. :thumbsup:
